analysis.overall: You spent 90% of the day in range with a solid average of 118 mg/dL, though a couple of stacked correction doses caused sharp dips late last night and overnight.

events.title: Post-dinner low
events.description: Adding a small correction bolus shortly after dinner combined with active insulin, dropping you down to 53 mg/dL before a 23g carb treatment brought you back up.

events.title: Overnight correction drop
events.description: Multiple small micro-corrections given between midnight and 2:50 AM accumulated and triggered a fast drop down to 69 mg/dL.

events.title: Breakfast rollercoaster
events.description: Insulin hit faster than your 60g breakfast carbs, causing a temporary dip to 77 mg/dL followed by a quick bounce up to 152 mg/dL.

events.title: Smooth lunch handling
events.description: A 4.8u dose for 70g of carbs kept your glucose steady, peaking gently at 161 mg/dL before settling into range.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Watch out for stacking small correction boluses when sitting between 140–160 mg/dL, as the overlapping insulin tends to cause sudden drops 2–3 hours later.
